texts.preamble: Ashwani Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:51311) on 13 December, 2024
texts.facts: The petitioner has challenged quashing of the entire proceeding pending against the petitioner for accusation of committing offence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
texts.arguments: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the statutory right given to the accused petitioner could not be availed because of the samples could not be sent to the Central Laboratory before its expiry, and therefore, continuance of further proceeding against the petitioner would be an abuse of process of law. 3. On the contrary, learned counsel for the State would contend that the petitioner can very well agitate the issue before the trial Court at a subsequent stage and it is further contended that there is concurrent finding of two Courts below, therefore, no case is made out in favour of the petitioner. [2024:RJ-JD:51311] (2 of 3) [CRLMP-4424/2022] 4. Heard learned counsel for both the parties. Ashwani Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:51311) on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44899795/ 1 5. 7. The law in this regard is not more res integra in light of the judgment passed by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Girishbhai Dahyabhai Shah Vs. C.C. Jani And Anr. (2009(15) SCC, in which Hon'ble the Supreme Court has propounded that seeking further analysis of the sample is an absolute statutory right of an accused and depriving him from making any prayer in this regard certainly infringes his statutory right and therefore, the proceedings were [LEAKAGE_MASK] in the matter.
